prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: no delight. Baking on tarmac at #MSP. Gate change. No air in plane. Eveyone sweating. This is gross.
Delta: I sincerely apologize for the uncomfortable conditions onboard.   *HML

Customer: check your DMs please thanks
Delta: Hi, Joshua. My apologies for any confusion. Allow me a few minutes to review your reservation. *HJH

Customer: Frustrated with . I pay to check bag which is overhead size & they let people check for free at gate & boarding process, cluster F.
Delta: The gate agent may request baggage check due to the weight and balance of the aircraft. It's for safety reasons. *ALS

Customer: arrived with priority baggage broken & screws sticking out the side. I am told this is “normal wear & tear” and no repairs. Not OK. https://t.co/6ZHXjj5aKu
Delta: We apologize for the inconvenience. Here is the link, please follow the instructions:  https://t.co/XwO5qwnsan *AFM

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: praise):
"""has a bowl with free mints, jolly ranchers, and werther’s originals at the baggage check. surprise & delight, y’all!"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Thank you for sharing the sweet surprise! We’re delighted you enjoyed the treats at baggage check. Your feedback brightens our day.
